title: The Influence of Financial Literacy, Income Level, and Social Environment on Generation Z's Saving Behavior
authors: Dewi, N.P.; Anggraeni, N.L.; Suardana, I.W.; Dwijaksana, E.I.
tldr: A quantitative study of 200 Indonesian Gen Z individuals finds that financial literacy has the strongest positive influence on saving behavior, followed by income level and social environment, with financial literacy moderating the relationship between income and savings.
problem_and_motivation: Generation Z exhibits lower savings rates compared to previous generations despite growing access to financial products, attributed to impulsive spending habits and limited financial understanding. There is limited research specifically examining how financial literacy, income level, and social environment collectively influence Gen Z saving behavior in Indonesian urban contexts, particularly in Denpasar City.
approach: Administered structured questionnaires to 200 Gen Z respondents (born 1997-2012) in Denpasar City.
Used judgment sampling with criteria: Gen Z age, minimum 1-year residency, and willingness to participate.
Measured financial literacy using financial knowledge questions and self-assessed understanding.
Assessed income level through self-reported monthly income categories.
Evaluated social environment using peer and family financial influence scales.
Measured saving behavior through self-reported savings frequency and amount.
Performed multiple regression analysis to determine factor influences.
Tested moderating effect of financial literacy on the income-savings relationship.
findings: Financial literacy has the strongest positive influence on Gen Z saving behavior (β=0.412, p<0.001).
Income level significantly influences saving behavior (β=0.298, p<0.001).
Social environment positively influences saving behavior (β=0.187, p<0.01).
Financial literacy moderates the relationship between income level and saving behavior.
All three factors combined explain 62.3% of variance in Gen Z saving behavior.
Higher financial literacy amplifies the positive effect of income on savings.
Peer influence can either promote or hinder saving behavior depending on financial literacy levels.
Financial education interventions show potential for improving Gen Z savings outcomes.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Respondent Characteristics → 55% female, majority 20-24 years, students and early-career professionals.
Table 2: Validity and Reliability Tests → All items significant (p<0.05) with Cronbach's Alpha >0.70.
Table 3: Multiple Regression Results → Financial literacy β=0.412, income β=0.298, social environment β=0.187.
Table 4: Moderating Effect Analysis → Financial literacy significantly moderates income-savings relationship.
Figure 1: Research Model → Shows direct and moderated paths from predictors to saving behavior.

key_equations.explanation: Multiple regression model predicting saving behavior (Y) from financial literacy (X1), income (X2), and social environment (X3).
Moderated regression model testing financial literacy as moderator of income-savings relationship.
Combined model explains 62.3% of variance in Gen Z saving behavior.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This quantitative study provides empirical evidence that financial literacy is the strongest predictor of Gen Z saving behavior in Indonesia, significantly moderating the relationship between income level and savings. It demonstrates that all three factors (financial literacy, income, social environment) collectively explain 62.3% of saving behavior variance, and reveals that peer influence can either promote or hinder savings depending on financial literacy levels, offering insights for targeted financial education interventions.
directly_justifies: Financial literacy is the strongest positive predictor of Gen Z saving behavior (β=0.412).
Financial literacy moderates the income-savings relationship, amplifying the effect of income on savings.
Social environment positively influences saving behavior but can be undermined by low financial literacy.
Combined factors explain 62.3% of variance in Gen Z saving behavior.
Peer influence can either promote or hinder savings depending on financial literacy levels.
limits: Geographic limitation to Denpasar City, Indonesia.
Self-reported data may introduce recall and social desirability bias.
Judgment sampling limits generalizability to broader Gen Z population.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) received high relevance as the core study profiles Gen Z financial behaviors. Domain 7 (Budgeting/Savings) received high relevance for its focus on saving behavior and goal formulation. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) received low relevance for contextualizing Gen Z financial landscape. Domains 1-3, 6, 8-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, predictive modeling, anomaly detection, privacy, engagement, mobile design, or synthetic data generation.

limitations: Judgment sampling not representative of all Gen Z.
